title: How do so many AI games have decent live2D/animation?
author: Low_Break8983
selftext:
I've been trying to make AI games for a while now and it's going well enough. Managed to get decent results from coding AIs, music AIs, and even image generation AIs. But the one area I consistently struggle with is animation. It's extra frustrating because I've seen dozens, maybe even hundreds of AI games at this point that have very low quality images, much worse than what I could generate, but then their live2D animations are 100x better than what I could make. Transparency, high quality jiggle physics, realistic flowing hair. I notice a lot of this especially on adult game found on sites like patreon and similar. They'll have mediocre AI images and music but then have full blown animated adult scenes and I don't understand how they're achieving those results. 



I've tried every major video generation service and even sprite service and I can't even come close to the live2D animations I find in most animated AI games, even ones made 6 months ago. Does anyone have any advice? 

  
(And before you suggest any of the services advertised in this sub, I've already tried most of them so I can tell you it's not any of the stuff being shilled on reddit unfortunately (shout out to the mods for also stopping all of the advertisement spam in this sub))

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body:
Me personally I use Gemini for creating a outline then use a free web pixel art editor to touch up the generation and animate it by hand, I also use gemini sometimes to generate sprite sheets and do the same method (touch up & add) 

When I get some of my current projects finished up I plan on making a free with ads web application with this work flow all on one page. As I totally agree there isn't a perfect AI sprite sheet generator.

comments.body: If ur good at math n terminology u can get much better results

comments.author: MTOMalley
comments.body: Just trigonometry and layering, go ask AI to generate you a spline editor, or some bone-based sprite animation and I'm sure you'll get there in no time.

comments.author: bunnyhome
comments.body:
i think they use the built-in physics constraints in Spline or Live2D for the hair and boob jiggle, it's not animated by hand. it's the same physics as livestreaming VTuber models. i think they probably just bought a rig beforehand, swap the textures on, then animate the body and arms to move and let the physics handle the rest.  
  
another possible automated workflow is:  
1. separate the body parts from an image (Segment Anything Model)  
2. generate rigging data from video with a person in it (MediaPipe)  
3. resolve the rigging data to Live2D (KalidoKit)
